answer: An operator’s kth identity needs a bridge with k sponsors outside its cluster, each signing one crystal into the bridge and locking one timber behind it until that identity is judged. The bridge spends each crystal, so a sponsor backs only one identity anywhere. The first identity costs one sponsor and one timber, the tenth ten of each, the thousandth a thousand; a thousand clones need 500,500 sponsor slots holding 500,500 timber. The attacker’s bill is those bribes plus capital frozen in timber.
